newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-GWR to complete Classic deal in December.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-GWR to complete Classic deal in December.

text.p: Fast-growing UK commercial radio operator GWR Group Plc expects to complete its acquisition of Classic FM Plc in December, Chief Executive Ralph Bernard said on Friday.
Bernard said GWR was working on the disposal of some smaller licences in order to comply with ownership restrictions once it merged with Classic but he saw no further regulatory hurdles.

GWR announced in August that it planned to acquire the rest of UK national broadcaster Classic, in which it had a 17 percent stake, for a total of 71.5 million stg. Under the deal, music company EMI will acquire a 10 percent stake in GWR.

Classic FM chairman Sir Peter Michael will have a nine percent stake in GWR. Harmsworth Media and Capital Radio, existing GWR shareholders, will retain stakes of 19.8 percent and 13 percent respectively.

"We won't sell our core, high-earning stations but there has been a reasonable amount of interest in one or two of our smaller stations," Bernard told Reuters. Speculation has centred on stations in St Albans, just north of London, and King's Lynn, in eastern England.
Bernard said action would be taken at Classic to ensure "loss makers are turned into profit makers very quickly."

Classic FM, which has operations in the Netherlands, Sweden and Finland, had pre-tax losses of 2.8 million stg in the year to November 1995 -- the largest slice of which came from its Dutch arm. Bernard said that the UK operation made a profit of around one million stg.
He said that an urgent review of its Dutch unit would be carried out and that its sale would have to be considered if a prospective buyer emerged.
The chief executive was speaking after GWR posted pre-tax profit of 8.2 million stg, an increase of 55 percent, in the year to end September.

Bernard said that GWR's advertising revenue had grown at around 12 percent this year, a figure which he said was slightly below the industry average as the company worked to integrate a number of acquisitions.
Looking ahead, Bernard said that he thought radio advertising would continue to expand apace.
"I still feel pretty confident about the future. We are not going to see the 30-plus percent growth of two or three years ago but growth well into double figures is on the cards."
